query: How does resolution time vary by agent and issue type?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: The core metric the query is about; per-incident duration is exactly the right axis for comparing agents and issue types. However, groundedness is shaky: the row samples expose only opened_at implicitly plus identical sys_updated_on/closed_at timestamps, yet produced values like 286.79 or 348.57 hours cannot be derived from the shown source snippets (closed_at equals sys_updated_on). The value must come from opened_at-to-closed_at, which is plausible from the full schema, but the evidence samples do not corroborate the specific figures, and a 22-row NULL rate suggests missing derivations.

per_column.name: agent_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: A per-agent average directly serves the 'by agent' half of the query, giving a clean grouping axis. It is a deterministic aggregate of resolution_hours over assigned_to, so it is well grounded given the source columns; only mild redundancy with what a groupby would compute keeps usefulness below top.

per_column.name: category_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Per-category average serves the 'by issue type' half of the query. It is a straightforward aggregate over the existing category column and resolution_hours, so it is sound; slight redundancy with a native groupby limits it.

per_column.name: agent_category_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: The agent-by-category interaction average is the most on-target column for 'how resolution time varies by agent AND issue type,' offering the joint grouping the query explicitly calls for. It is a warranted aggregate of derivable values.

judge.rationale: All four columns target exactly the axes the query asks about: a per-incident resolution duration plus agent, category, and agent-by-category rollups. Together they provide genuine analytical leverage for the comparison. Groundedness is generally strong because the aggregates derive deterministically from resolution_hours over existing category/assigned_to columns; the main weakness is resolution_hours itself, whose specific per-row values are not corroborated by the evidence samples (identical closed_at/sys_updated_on timestamps and a high NULL count), indicating some values may not be soundly derivable from the shown source text.
